problem: A pressurized cell sheared at yield sees its loading rate rise tenfold. Rate-and-state friction jumps by $a\ln10$, then decays over the slip distance $D_c$ to the new steady state ($b>a$: velocity weakening).
result: DES follows its exact discrete recursion to round-off at every step (state and friction identical, stress within 9e-16), so the state is updated once per physical time step, not once per PT iteration. Against the continuum solution the largest friction error after the step is 9.56e-04, 4.67e-04, 2.31e-04, 1.15e-04 for steps of 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 s: first order, against a jump of 0.0230.
scope: 2D unit cell with every node prescribed, so equilibrium and mesh errors cannot enter; EP-RSF, aging law, $a=0.01$, $b=0.015$, $D_c=0.001$ m, slip rate $V=2w\dot\epsilon_{II}$ (total-strain-rate projection); confinement 1 MPa, pore pressure 0.8 MPa, cohesion 100 kPa. The rate step is a restart from the last checkpoint with the new boundary velocity, which also checks that the state variable survives restart. Not covered: slip-law evolution, the maximum-shear projection, stick-slip instability and coupling of friction to flow or dilation. (a) friction; (b) stress; (c) step convergence.
meaning: This verifies the evolving rate-and-state friction of the effective-stress plasticity, which the strength page checks only at constant friction.
